extracted.intended_audience: GAP core developers and prospective contributors (people submitting code, tests, or documentation to the GAP project)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for contributing code, tests, and documentation to the GAP project: branch usage, backporting, pull request procedure, code formatting, CI/testing, and vendored-dependency maintenance. Intended as a reference manual for developers working on GAP's repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branching policy (master vs stable-4.X)
rubrics_metrics.description: By default all changes go into the master branch. Releases of the 4.X.* series are made from the stable-4.X branch (where X is some number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use master for new changes and pull requests by default. Only the most recent release branch is used for releases; older release branches are kept around but new releases are not normally made from them. Branch protection is enabled on primary branches so direct pushes are restricted; all changes should go through pull requests so tests run automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backporting process for release branches
rubrics_metrics.description: To get changes into the stable-4.X release branch after they have landed on master, use a backport label workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add the backport-to-4.X label to a merged PR (ask someone with permission to add it if needed). Sometime after merge and before the next stable release, maintainers will open backporting PRs (possibly grouping multiple PRs). After a PR has been backported, replace backport-to-4.X with backport-to-4.X-DONE to avoid reprocessing and to aid changelog-generation scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making direct changes to the release branch
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct changes to stable-4.X are allowed when changes are only for stable-4.X and not suitable for master (e.g., divergence makes backporting impractical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a pull request which targets stable-4.X (select target branch on GitHub). When doing so, explain in the PR description why the change must target the release branch rather than master.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code formatting baseline rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple formatting rules: no tabs; no trailing whitespace; all source files should end with a newline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are automatically enforced if your editor honors the repository .editorconfig. For historical reasons there is no further strict formatting standard — adapt your changes to the surrounding code (e.g., match existing indentation). Avoid large-scale reformatting while editing; if you must reformat, do it in a separate commit that only contains formatting changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting tools and kernel code formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: For completely new kernel code in C/C++ use clang-format. For edits, use git clang-format to reformat only modified code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can use git clang-format (which reformats only code already modified). When necessary, the command git clang-format $(git merge-base master) can help format just the code you modified. Nevertheless, avoid large-scale reformatting and keep reformatting in separate commits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pull request workflow and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions should be made via GitHub pull requests; by default target master. The CI test suite runs automatically for PRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus your pull request: ideally don't change multiple unrelated things in one PR (this makes review easier). Read code formatting rules before submitting. Use labels to help generate release notes and categorize changes (see label guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling pull requests for release notes and backports
rubrics_metrics.description: Use labels to aid release-note generation and to request backports or indicate the kind of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always add one of the 'release notes' labels. If the change should be backported to a stable branch, add a 'backports' label. Consider adding a 'kind' label to indicate whether the change is a bug fix, enhancement, or other. Other labels are optional and can help categorize things for release notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous integration (CI) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP uses GitHub Actions to run the GAP test suite for every commit to primary branches and for all pull requests in order to detect regressions early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which tests are run is controlled by .github/workflows/CI.yml and .github/workflows/release.yml. See GitHub Actions documentation for syntax. Also consult dev/ci.sh and dev/ci-*.sh for scripts executed as part of CI tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing suites and how to run them locally
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP's test suite is split into multiple parts: testinstall (quick), teststandard (slower but more comprehensive), testextra (very slow), and testbugfix (small tests for specific bugfixes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run via the GAP executable with the respective test files: ./gap tst/testinstall.g, ./gap tst/teststandard.g, ./gap tst/testextra.g, and ./gap tst/testbugfix.g. Choose the appropriate suite depending on frequency and comprehensiveness needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression tracking using bisect helper
rubrics_metrics.description: Use dev/bisect.sh to track down which commit introduced a regression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The script can be very helpful; read the extensive comments in the file to learn its usage and options before running it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendored dependencies management
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP includes copies of some third-party software (vendored) to ease building GAP with minimal external dependencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: extern/gmp (GMP), extern/zlib (zlib), hpcgap/extern/gc (Boehm GC), hpcgap/extern/libatomic_ops (libatomic_ops). Maintain these copies when updating — maintainers may update them from time to time. Special files cnf/config.guess and cnf/config.sub are used by configure and can be updated via cnf/update-config.sh; autoconf/autoreconf should ideally install latest versions but may not always do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion and communication channels
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP uses Slack and an open developer mailing list for discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everyone can join Slack via https://gap-system.org/slack. There is also an open developer list with low volume; subscribe at https://lists.uni-kl.de/gap/info/gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release process reference and changelog generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases are made from the most recent release branch; release details are documented in dev/releases/README.md.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling (see label guidance) helps scripts that generate changelog updates for releases. Do not expect new releases from older release branches after a newer one exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR scope and reviewability guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep pull requests focused to make reviewing easier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid changing multiple unrelated things in one PR. If you must reformat code, place that in a separate commit. Provide clear explanations in PR descriptions (especially when targeting release branches or making non-obvious changes).
